title: Gap Cluster 01 DRILL: Cell Signalling
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 6 questions · 56 marks · 16 parts · one mark per minute, so about an hour · every question lifted from a real paper
los_html:
What this gap drill covers, gap by gap. The mend doc closes them; these questions test them.
B3-1 amplification against activationQ2(a)
B3-2 temporary weak bonds hold both complexesQ1
B3-3 receptor and enzyme both reused and unchangedQ1
B3-4 binding site against active siteQ1
B3-5 an enzyme lowers activation energy, a receptor does notQ1
B3-6 hormone unchanged, substrate becomes productQ1
B3-7 a GPLR is a cell surface receptormend doc only, no question requires an intracellular receptor
B3-8 the two requirements for amplificationQ2(b)
B3-9 glycogen synthase makes glycogenQ6, and the naming discipline again in Q5(a)
B3-10 insulin moves glucose into the cellQ6
B3-11 RTK is receptor tyrosine kinaseQ3(e), Q6
B3-12 IP₃, not IP₂Q4(b), Q4(c)
B3-13 cyclic AMP activates PKA; DAG plus calcium activates PKCQ4(a) against Q4(b)
B3-14 autophosphorylation on the cytoplasmic tailQ6
decay-prone: the GPLR working principleQ3(a)
decay-prone: the RTK working principleQ6
decay-prone: the three termination enzymesQ3(c), Q5(a), Q5(d)
decay-prone: nature and roles of second messengersQ3(b)

Duplicate check on the answers, not the labels. Only Q6 requires the RTK activation sequence. Only Q3(a) requires the GPLR activation sequence; Q4(a) starts downstream of adenylyl cyclase and Q5(a) is handed the glucagon cascade in its stem. Only Q1 requires the receptor against enzyme points. Q3(c) names phosphodiesterase as a shut-off enzyme and Q5(d) asks you to predict what happens when it is blocked, which is the one fact that appears in two questions, under two different demands.
